content: 1. Letermovir and Nifedipine: Letermovir increases nifedipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4 metabolism in the liver and intestines. Use caution and monitor closely for potential adverse effects. 2. Letermovir and Nirogacestat: Letermovir significantly increases nirogacestat levels by affecting CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, monitor closely for toxicity. 3. Letermovir and Nisoldipine: Letermovir raises nisoldipine levels through CYP3A4 inhibition. Exercise caution and monitor closely for side effects. 4. Letermovir and Nitrendipine: Letermovir increases nitrendipine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 5. Letermovir and Norethindrone: Letermovir elevates norethindrone levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 6. Letermovir and Norgestrel: Letermovir increases norgestrel levels and effects by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Strong or moderate CYP3A4 inhibitors may further increase systemic norgestrel concentrations, raising the risk of adverse effects. 7. Letermovir and Oliceridine: Letermovir increases oliceridine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Modify therapy and monitor closely. If coadministration is necessary, reduce oliceridine dosing frequency. Monitor for respiratory depression and sedation, and adjust subsequent doses accordingly. If the inhibitor is discontinued, consider increasing the oliceridine dose until stable effects are achieved. Monitor for signs of opioid withdrawal. 8. Letermovir and Olmesartan: Letermovir increases olmesartan levels by inhibiting OATP1B1/3 transporters. Use caution and monitor closely. Letermovir, as an OATP1B1/3 inhibitor, may increase plasma concentrations of coadministered OATP1B1/3 substrates. 9. Letermovir and Omaveloxolone: Letermovir significantly increases omaveloxolone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the omaveloxolone dose to 100 mg/day and monitor closely for adverse effects. If side effects occur, further reduce the dose to 50 mg/day. 10. Letermovir and Ombitasvir/Paritaprevir/Ritonavir & Dasabuvir (DSC): This combination increases letermovir levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of letermovir, an OATP1B1/3 substrate, with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 11. Letermovir and Omeprazole: Letermovir increases omeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose adjustments may be necessary. 12. Letermovir and Ondansetron: Letermovir raises ondansetron levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 13. Letermovir and Oxcarbazepine: Oxcarbazepine decreases letermovir levels by inducing UGT1A1/3 enzymes. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of letermovir with UGT1A1/3 inducers is not recommended. 14. Letermovir and Oxybutynin: Letermovir increases oxybutynin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 15. Letermovir and Oxycodone: Letermovir elevates oxycodone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 16. Letermovir and Paclitaxel: Paclitaxel increases letermovir levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Letermovir also increases paclitaxel levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Monitor closely for toxicity. 17. Letermovir and Pacritinib: Letermovir significantly increases pacritinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 18. Letermovir and Palovarotene: Letermovir increases palovarotene levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with moderate CYP3A inhibitors. If unavoidable, reduce the palovarotene dose by 50% and monitor closely. 19. Letermovir and Pantoprazole: Letermovir raises pantoprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. Dose adjustments may be necessary. 20. Letermovir and Pazopanib: Pazopanib increases letermovir levels by reducing its metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. Coadministration of letermovir with OATP1B1/3 inhibitors may increase letermovir plasma concentrations. 21. Letermovir and Pemigatinib: Letermovir significantly increases pemigatinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the pemigatinib dose as per the drug monograph. After discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives, resume the previous pemigatinib dose. 22. Letermovir and Pexidartinib: Letermovir increases pexidartinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the pexidartinib dose as per the drug monograph. Resume the previous dose after discontinuing the CYP3A4 inhibitor for three elimination half-lives. 23. Letermovir and Phenobarbital: Phenobarbital decreases letermovir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Coadministration of letermovir with P-gp inducers is not recommended. 24. Letermovir and Phenytoin: Phenytoin decreases letermovir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 25. Letermovir and Pimozide: Letermovir increases pimozide levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of QT prolongation and torsades de pointes. 26. Letermovir and Pioglitazone: Letermovir and pioglitazone may increase each other's levels. Use caution and monitor glucose levels closely. 27. Letermovir and Pitavastatin: Letermovir increases pitavastatin levels significantly. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis, especially when combined with cyclosporine. 28. Letermovir and Pravastatin: Letermovir increases pravastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Monitor closely for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. When coadministered with cyclosporine, the pravastatin dose should not exceed 20 mg/day. 29. Letermovir and Pretomanid: Pretomanid increases letermovir levels. Use caution and monitor closely for drug-related adverse effects. 30. Letermovir and Primidone: Primidone decreases letermovir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 31. Letermovir and Progesterone (Micronized/Natural): Letermovir increases progesterone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 32. Letermovir and Propafenone: Letermovir increases propafenone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 33. Letermovir and Propranolol: Letermovir enhances propranolol effects by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 34. Letermovir and Quetiapine: Letermovir increases quetiapine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 35. Letermovir and Quinidine: Letermovir increases quinidine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 36. Letermovir and Quinine: Letermovir increases quinine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 37. Letermovir and Rabeprazole: Letermovir increases rabeprazole levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 38. Letermovir and Ramelteon: Letermovir increases ramelteon levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 39. Letermovir and Ranolazine: Letermovir increases ranolazine levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 40. Letermovir and Repaglinide: Letermovir increases repaglinide levels. Avoid coadministration, especially with cyclosporine, due to the risk of hypoglycemia. 41. Letermovir and Repotrectinib: Letermovir increases repotrectinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. Discontinue CYP3A inhibitors and wait 3-5 elimination half-lives before initiating repotrectinib. 42. Letermovir and Ribociclib: Letermovir increases ribociclib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 43. Letermovir and Rifampin: Rifampin decreases letermovir levels by inducing P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporters. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. 44. Letermovir and Rifaximin: Letermovir increases rifaximin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 45. Letermovir and Rimegepant: Letermovir increases rimegepant levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid repeating rimegepant doses within 48 hours if coadministered with a moderate CYP3A4 inhibitor. 46. Letermovir and Risperidone: Letermovir increases risperidone levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 47. Letermovir and Ritonavir: Ritonavir increases letermovir levels by reducing its metabolism. Letermovir also increases ritonavir levels via CYP3A4 inhibition. Use caution and monitor closely. 48. Letermovir and Rivaroxaban: Letermovir increases rivaroxaban levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 49. Letermovir and Rosiglitazone: Letermovir increases rosiglitazone levels. Use caution and monitor glucose concentrations closely. 50. Letermovir and Rosuvastatin: Letermovir increases rosuvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Monitor closely for myopathy and rhabdomyolysis. When coadministered with cyclosporine, the rosuvastatin dose should not exceed 5 mg/day. 51. Letermovir and Salmeterol: Letermovir increases salmeterol levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 52. Letermovir and Saxagliptin: Letermovir increases saxagliptin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 53. Letermovir and Seladelpar: Letermovir increases seladelpar levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution in patients who are poor CYP2C9 metabolizers and are coadministered a moderate/strong CYP3A4 inhibitor. 54. Letermovir and Selumetinib: Letermovir increases selumetinib levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration or use an alternative drug. If unavoidable, reduce the selumetinib dose as per the drug monograph. 55. Letermovir and Sertraline: Letermovir increases sertraline levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 56. Letermovir and Sildenafil: Letermovir increases sildenafil levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Use caution and monitor closely. 57. Letermovir and Simvastatin: Letermovir significantly increases simvastatin levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Coadministration is contraindicated due to the risk of myopathy or rhabdomyolysis, especially when combined with cyclosporine. 58. Letermovir and Siponimod: Letermovir increases siponimod levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Avoid coadministration with moderate or strong CYP3A4 inhibitors plus moderate or strong CYP2C9 inhibitors. 59. Letermovir and Sirolimus: Letermovir increases sirolimus levels by inhibiting CYP3A4. Monitor sirolimus plasma concentrations during treatment and after discontinuation of letermovir. Adjust the sirolimus dose accordingly. When coadministered with cyclosporine, sirolimus should be taken 4 hours after cyclosporine administration. Higher sirolimus doses may be needed if cyclosporine is discontinued.
